utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, let me simplify things to the extreme. Carla Del Ponte was the Chief Prosecutor of the International Tribunal for many years. After leaving the Tribunal, she published a memoir. In one sentence, she said that at the time, the prime minister in the Serbian government, I add "the mafia prime minister," Zoran Djindjic said, "Take Seselj and don't send him back." And after that, she issued an indictment, and then I came to The Hague of my own accord. For me, that is an admission of a flagrant violation of the duties of a Prosecutor. I'm not making a political speech, as Mr. Mundis said at our last hearing. I'm just limiting myself to the legal extract from that book and what follows from it. If that is true, then she's liable to criminal responsibility, and then the Trial Chamber must take a position regarding the validity of such a statement, because it leads to many consequences. Then you can see how come you have false witnesses, the way in which they tell their story, and so on. But I think it is absolutely indispensable for the Trial Chamber to take a position. And to begin with, I think you should give instructions for the relevant portions of the book to be translated into English and French, in fact all parts of the book in which my name is mentioned. Perhaps that would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I haven't read the book either, and I'm not in a position to comment fully on the correctness of the accused's interpretation of the one sentence that he's talking about. The correct legal remedy in this situation, if the accused wants to do something, is to make a motion alleging that there have been some sort of abuse of prosecutorial power. That's what he should do. Your Honours directed that, I think, last week, that if he wanted to raise these sort of matters, it should be done in the form of a motion. I think that's absolutely correct. And if the accused thinks that there's a link between those events and false evidence being presented in court, he must also prove that and substantiate it. Last week, the accused alleged that Prosecution counsel knowingly is putting false evidence before this Trial Chamber. There must be some sort of -- sorry, of substantiation of those kind of allegations. If the accused has evidence that he wants to put before the Trial Chamber on this issue, he should do so, but continuing to raise this in this manner is inappropriate, in my respectful submission. And if you want a translation of any parts of the book, he can use the translation services of the Tribunal just as well as the Chamber or the Prosecution can, so he can identify the passages he wants translated and have them translated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I believe that Mr. Marcussen has identified the problem very well. If you're challenging, legally, and let's remain in the legal context, if you're legally contesting anything to do with the book, the report -- the rapport or the links that Mrs. Del Ponte had with the former Prime Minister Djindjic, so if you're contesting those links and the indictment, if I understand correctly, would be tainted because -- in a way because the indictment would be, according to you, carried out according to a request made by the prime minister at the time, you would have to put down in writing, black on white, by way of a motion so that the Trial Chamber be seized by this motion. The Prosecutor, of course, as well can answer or reply if the indictment is contested or challenged, and then the Trial Chamber will render a decision. You must understand that this cannot be done orally. We must follow the administrative ways. You have the right, and Mr. Marcussen recognises it. He says that if in the book some excerpts concern you, you have the right, by way of a motion, to request that those passages be translated to you in your own language so that you can back your submission. This is a possibility that you have. You're saying that you're expecting something from the Trial Chamber, and I am telling you that we will intervene if -- or after receiving your submissions, your arguments, and after receiving also the submissions presented by the Prosecutor. At this point in time, I am not excluding anything. I'm also -- I could even ask Mrs. Carla Del Ponte to come and explain what she meant. Nothing is impossible, but I am expecting you to present your submissions. You have a team that works with you. They can very well draft this motion. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think what happened as a problem by far exceeds the interests of one accused in one case. Of course, I am able already by tomorrow to prepare a written filing, and they will do that and I will fax it to you tomorrow. However, I'm drawing attention to two very major issues which do not affect only my interests in this case, but unless there is a reaction to them, they undermine the entire Tribunal. I remind you of Article 16 of the Statute, and it says that the Prosecutor must act independently as a separate body of the International Tribunal. He may not ask or receive instructions from any government or any other source. That is what the Statute says. And in the book by Carla Del Ponte, it says: "Djindjic, in connection with Seselj, has sent me only one request. 'Take him away and don't send him back again.'" This is stated in Carla Del Ponte's book. This is not a question of my interests in this case, but as regards my interest, I will submit my submissions already tomorrow. But this is of far greater importance for this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will then be seized with a motion. Mr. Marcussen, did you want to say something? No, you're sitting down. Very well. Mr. Seselj, do you have another issue to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only if this may be of interest to you. I can give you a copy of the statement of Witness VS-1031, addressed to my legal associates. I now have the original of the statement with the original stamp, and a few copies if this may be of interest to you. This is my first contact with this witness by my legal assistants. And I also have a copy for a representative of the Prosecution. If you wish to have a copy, I could ask the usher to be kind enough to give it to you. One can see here that he stated that after Ramush Haradinaj was acquitted on the 3rd of April, he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, VS-1031 certainly benefits from protective measures. Let's not disclose any names which would enable to identify the person. You are handing me a statement signed by his own hand, in your own -- in your language, which I don't speak. I don't know what this contains. It's not 1031, it's 031, it's Witness VS-031.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I won't mention his name at all. I just draw your attention to a sentence where he says that on the 3rd of April, he learned that Haradinaj was acquitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: There's no basis for the accused to read out any parts of a statement from a witness who is to testify before the Court without the witness being here. If there's some procedural point the accused wants to raise, he can do that, but we're once again in a situation where the accused reads out statements that have been presented to him. It's completely out of context, and the accused should make some proper use of court time and not read out these sort of statements in this way in the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, you are producing this document. It is not necessary to read, of course, this document, but what are you getting at, exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted the Trial Chamber to decide what to do, whether they will continue to insist on this witness being a Prosecution witness, or whether he'll be a Defence witness, or no witness at all. As far as I know, you issued a subpoena for this witness. Is that right? I'm not quite certain about that, but I think so. Whether there was this formal pressure in the form of a subpoena or pressure from the Prosecution, he was due to come here last week. I don't know exactly what happened, but clearly one can see from this statement that under no circumstances will he be a witness for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It might seem an odd request, but in light of the impact that some of these statements have on witnesses outside the courtroom, I would respectfully ask the Trial Chamber if we can redact this part of what has just been going on in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me consult with my fellow Judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Trial Chamber has deliberated on this and is deciding not to redact what has just been said. However, the Trial Chamber would like to indicate that whenever it is running into a problem that it becomes aware of, either through the Prosecution, through the witness, or through the accused, the Trial Chamber rules on this. There can be different decisions, there's different solutions. It can be a contempt of court, a subpoena, wait and see. There are different solutions. And as of now, we have not decided anything, so there is no reason to mention the problem. You attracted our attention on a new element, and we will incorporate it when we assess the problem, but as of now we have not decided anything. Therefore, please move on to another topic. If you have no other topic to raise, I have a question for you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is my last question. Last week, you briefly said something, and I did not have time to ask you some more information on this, because we were running out of time, and this came right after a good number of other events. But out of memory, I can say that last week, after different problems connected with cross-examination and the 92 ter, Rule 92 ter, you said that you envisaged -- that you were going to - I don't really know what you wanted, but you said that if need be, you were thinking of not showing any evidence when you were presenting your own case. This is what I understood at least, and I wondered whether this had to do with Rule 92 ter, or whether this has to do with something else, or whether you believe that at this stage, there was no need to present any evidence. You were not clear enough, and I did not really understand, so could you please explain what you meant at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as opposed to some Prosecution witnesses who have a perfect memory and remember all the details which occurred 15 or 16 years ago, my memory is not quite so precise. But as far as I can remember, I didn't link this possibility only to 92 ter witnesses, and surely this can be found in the transcript, but I said if you continue to take away Defence witnesses, and unless the problem of financing is resolved, there is a possibility that there will not be a Defence case. I wasn't emphatic, nor was it a decision. I said that this was a possibility, something that I had started to think about. My Defence team has still not made a final decision about this, and to the best of my recollection, I have now explained what it is I intimated last week. May I repeat once again, if there are many 92 ter witnesses, if you snatch away from me Defence witnesses, and there are already 20 of them that the Prosecution is counting on as their witnesses, though they have signed a statement saying that they would be Defence witnesses, and if the problem of financing is not resolved, it will not be possible to have a Defence case. And the last time we discussed finances, I said I wouldn't raise it again until we reached the Defence case stage. If it's not resolved by then, I don't see how I can produce evidence in my Defence. I already have great problems with my associates, because they're not receiving any remuneration, even though they're doing such a lot of hard work, more than any other Defence counsel. And trusting my word, they have been working very hard and very diligently, and now it appears that I have cheated them, I have misled them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Regarding the technical issue of financing your Defence, two or three weeks ago, I don't remember the exact date, the Trial Chamber took stock of the situation and it seems that this is how things stand at the moment. Registry was making some research on your indigency status, because all this can only work if the Registry notes -- the translation is not working? Very well. Obviously, there was a technical problem. Let me resume. Regarding this very technical issue of how your Defence is to be financed -- and while I'm talking I would like the usher to remove the blind because there's no need for the blind to be there. So regarding the very technical item of your -- financing of your Defence, two or three weeks ago, I can't remember the exact date, but the Trial Chamber took stock of the situation with the competent services at Registry, and according to the information we obtained, the Registrar was checking whether you were still an indigent through different steps, through a series of steps that the Registry is taking. This is a two-stage approach. The principle of payment is accepted, but before paying, the Registrar must absolutely make sure that you are truly indigent, and this is where there is a lock -- a checking system that the Registry is -- this is where the Registry is at. And obviously so far the Registrar has not -- is not convinced that you are fully indigent. So you may be fully indigent, partially indigent. I don't know what your financial status is. The Registrar has met with you, has sent you letters, and probably asked you to answer a number of questions put to you by him. The Trial Chamber is not meant to intervene in the everyday running of this Tribunal, except if at one point in time there is an infringement, a serious infringement of the rights of the Defence. In such a case, the Trial Chamber either proprio motu or on request can take steps and intervene, but as of now we have been told that they were checking whether you were truly indigent. This is where things stand at the moment. If they have proof that you cannot pay these sums because of your destitution, they will pay your associates. There's no problem there. This is the direct consequence of the decision made on how you are to finance your Defence, but the lock, because this is a true lock, is the question: Is Mr. Seselj truly indigent? And I think I'm reading between the lines, but I believe the Registrar so far has not been fully convinced that you are totally indigent. And the burden of proof, I'm sure you know this, the burden of proof is on you. The accused must absolutely demonstrate and prove that he is indigent. He has the onus of that. And obviously the Registrar so far seems to say that as things stand now, he is not fully convinced that you are truly indigent. This is where we stand now. For three or four weeks, the Trial Chamber has set this problem aside, because last time you told us officially that you would no longer raise it. But you've just raised it again, which obviously means that the problem has not been solved yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tell you that the question of determining whether you're indigent or not depends to a great extent on whether you fully collaborate with the Registry. You are to collaborate with the Registry to determine what your financial situation is. It all depends on you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Judges, I wouldn't have raised this issue at all, but I was only illustrating the reasons why I intimated that I might refrain from producing Defence evidence. I really think that the discussion regarding the financing of my Defence has been completed. Whatever I had to do with the Registrar, I did so by 2003. I will not collaborate by providing information about the property of members of my family. The fact that the Registrar doesn't believe me, doesn't trust me, it's up to him. That Registrar will never believe anything I say. You remember how I criticised him for his behaviour on the basis of the Milosevic transcript. There's the language of facts and there's the language of guesswork. According to the language of facts, he doesn't have any arguments to show that I'm capable of playing my Defence. What does it mean, that I am indigent? I have four children. Three are under age, and my wife is not working. So I'm not in a poor financial status in relation to conditions in Serbia, but not high enough for me to cover the costs of Defence in this Tribunal, which are much higher than in any national court. That is the situation. I am not poor, I am not so poor that I don't have bread to eat, but from what I have, nothing can be separated because the children would have nothing to eat. And the Registrar must provide a report about what he has found. Ever since 2003, he hasn't done it. A real study about it. He has done it in all the other cases. He hasn't done it in my case. I consider my cooperation with the Registrar completed. If he has evidence that I'm capable of paying my own Defence, let him produce the evidence. He undertook the investigation, not me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you're telling us that you have four children, four [as interpreted] that are still minor, and that your wife does not work. I assume that in your country, in Serbia, there are tax return files. I guess Serbian citizens pay their taxes when they have income. And even if they don't have any income, they have to file a tax return, an income tax report. I guess that your wife has to file an income tax report, just like you do. If you made this tax -- income tax return for 2005, 2006 and 2007, you must have a copy of them, and normally on the tax file, you know exactly what the financial standing of a person is. If, on this tax report, it says that neither your wife nor you can be taxed for income tax, it proves that you're indigent. Why won't you communicate a document of the kind to the Registry? This would prove that you are willing to collaborate to this procedure to find out whether you're indigent or not. The best solution would be for you to give the Registrar a copy of all your income tax reports. I'm sure that they would give an idea of your true situation, your true financial standing, because if the Registry has doubts on your real estate property, for example, or on your possible stocks that you may have, in case you had accounts -- bank accounts outside Serbia or if you had property outside Serbia, maybe in the countries where you lived for a few years, why don't you ask those banks to give you a certificate proving exactly how much money is on those bank accounts? Everything is very simple. Independently of your personal situation, with this position, you know, you're jeopardising four people who have been working for you. I'm not going to give any names, but everybody knows this, Mr. Krasic [Realtime transcript read in error "Krajisnik"] mainly, all these people who've been working for you. Or maybe they did this voluntarily and free of charge. I said Krasic, not Krajisnik, K-R-A-S-I-C. So maybe these people are waiting for a salary, and maybe it's the position that you've adopted that no payment is possible. To sum things up, you have the possibility of giving the Registry your income tax reports. This is probably very straightforward. And you could also send to the Registry your bank statements on your foreign bank accounts, if you have any. You cannot ask the Trial Chamber to become accountants or tax experts in order to check your financial standing. We could do this, but we have many other things to do, we have much more on our plate.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have provided all the figures to the Registrar in due course. It's a good thing that you raised the question of tax returns. In Serbia, there's a minimum on annual income below which no tax is payable, nor is it reported. My family and I were always below this minimum. We were never liable to taxes, neither me nor my family, when it comes to annual income. And the Registry has received from the state authorities in Serbia all the necessary information. There's really no need to discuss this matter further. I really wouldn't have raised it if you hadn't asked me about this possibility that I had mentioned of refraining from producing Defence evidence. I wouldn't have mentioned it, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's time to adjourn. We will resume tomorrow at 9.00 a.m., and this hearing will be devoted to the videos. I think there's about an hour and a half or two hours worth of videos, so that will keep us busy for the morning. Have a nice day, and we will resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 23rd day of April, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24
